key_insight: Maximally-Activating Example Metamodels (MAEMs) generate text examples designed to strongly activate a chosen direction inside a language model. This offers a way to interpret internal representations without being restricted to examples found in an existing text collection.
problem_solved: Searching a corpus for activating text can reveal only what that corpus contains, potentially missing examples that better explain a residual stream direction.
method: Supply a direction from a subject language model’s residual stream to a metamodel.
Use the metamodel to generate text exemplars intended to strongly activate that direction.
Optimize for cosine alignment with the supplied direction; the provided abstract is truncated before specifying the full objective.
impact: MAEMs could help interpretability practitioners explore internal model representations beyond fixed datasets. Generated examples offer clues about what a direction represents, rather than definitive explanations of its function.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: residual stream direction → MAEM → generated text → subject-model activation.
Side-by-side illustration of corpus search versus generated activating examples.
Vector diagram showing cosine alignment between a target direction and a text-induced activation.
Conceptual example cards linking internal directions to generated text, clearly labeled as illustrative.
paper_title: Towards interpreting any residual stream direction by scaling activation inversion
paper_authors: Celeste De Schamphelaere, Juan J. Vazquez, Ari Spiesberger, Tomáš Gavenčiak, Gavin Leech
